newsitem.title: UK: High sulphur fuel oil barges up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: High sulphur fuel oil barges up but off highs.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil barges ended the week higher, but off earlier highs. Traders said higher prices were paid for very prompt material early in the day, but low overall demand sapped the market.
High sulphur cargoes were also a touch weaker, with bids around the $83 cif mark, while one percent was offered a little higher with buying interest seen continuing.
High sulphur fuel barges were traded late between $87.50 and $88.50 after earlier trades at $89 fob ARA for RMG material.
Refinery product was traded early at $90 fob Rotterdam but later demand waned.
Thursday's close was $89.25/$89.50 for refinery material and ex-store was done at $87.50.
Some traders said that refinery material continued to be offered high at $90 but no buyers were seen at that number as the day progressed.
Low sulphur barges dipped a little with buyers and sellers at $94.50/$95.50 with no activity reported in the market.
High sulphur fuel cargoes were little talked except for some Russian material, with traders saying that most of the requirements were bunker geared at the moment.
But cargoes were assessed a little softer, with bids at $83 cif compared with $84 a day earlier.
"It's just a correction after barges moved down a little," one trader said.

One precent was offered a little higher at $96 fob after earlier trade this week at about $94.50, with sellers saying prompt barrels were on the low side at the moment. Some traders said lower quality material was in the $93/$94 range.
Buying interest came from players eyeing possible trans-Atlantic shipments with an open arbitrage to the United States, traders said.
